transcript.text: Hi everyone. The batch-inference service has passed staging validation on T4 GPUs, sustaining four concurrent inference jobs without failure, and it's ready for its first production workload. Before I can record the production operating plan, the launch-readiness checklist requires all four of us — platform, machine-learning, finance, and privacy — to review capacity, cost, and data-handling settings. I'd like to walk through each area so we can sign off. One thing to note upfront: our existing committed-use GPU credits can be applied to eligible A10G capacity provisioned in eu-west-1, which may be relevant for the capacity and cost discussion. Let's start with capacity — what do we need to cover?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from a separate production-sizing exercise I ran this afternoon. I measured eight concurrent inference jobs in the first customer workload and confirmed that the model exceeds T4 memory at that load. We need A10G GPUs with capacity for exactly eight concurrent jobs — not the four we validated in staging on T4s. This result hasn't been added to the launch ticket yet, so I'm flagging it now so it's part of the capacity and cost review.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have an important billing detail from today's cloud-account reconciliation that's directly relevant to Riley's eight-concurrent-job requirement. I confirmed that exactly six A10G GPU slots are covered by our existing committed-use credits, and the remaining two slots must be on-demand to stay within the approved hourly budget. This breakdown is still only in the finance worksheet, so I want it on the record now as we review capacity and cost together.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a critical data-handling restriction from a separate privacy assessment I conducted on the first workload's data-processing terms. I confirmed that the workload's records must remain in eu-west-1 and may not fail over to a US region under any circumstances. This regional restriction has not yet been attached to the launch ticket, so I'm flagging it now during the data-handling review. This is especially important given that we're discussing capacity and failover settings — any auto-scaling or failover configuration must be constrained to eu-west-1 only.
transcript.speaker: A4
